Three bedrooms with their own bathrooms, a real kitchen and plenty of space for the kids to play. Read more on our page for families.
Karaoke, PlayStation, a big living room and a rooftop BBQ: everything for long evenings together. Read more on our page for groups.
Space, privacy and a master bedroom of about 55 m² with its own balcony. A city break that feels like having your own home in Saigon.
WiFi up to 1 Gbit/s with mesh on every floor, quiet bedrooms and a dining table that doubles as a desk.

sections.h2: Living room: the heart of the house
p: The living room is where the day starts and where everyone ends up again in the evening. At about 40 m² it has room to spread out properly. The large L-shaped sofa seats the whole family or group at once, with space to put your feet up, and the 75-inch 4K TV makes it the natural place for a football match, a cartoon morning with the kids or a series everyone has been meaning to start. Netflix is ready to go.

After a hot day in the city, kick off your shoes, sink into the sofa and let someone put the kettle on in the kitchen. Plants and the glass doors keep the space light and relaxed rather than formal. It's a living room meant to be lived in: kids building a blanket fort on the sofa, friends planning tomorrow's route, someone curled up with a book in the corner.

A guest WC is right here in the living area, so visitors and kids don't have to climb the stairs to a bedroom bathroom. And with mesh WiFi of up to 1 Gbit/s, the living room also works as an easy place to answer a few emails or join a video call while the others are out exploring.

sections.h2: Kitchen and dining: cook like a local
p: Some of the best meals in Saigon start at the market. Bring back fresh herbs, mangoes and a bag of whatever smelled best at the street stall, and cook it your way in your own kitchen. It is fully equipped with a stove, an oven, a microwave, a rice cooker, a kettle and all the plates, bowls and cutlery you need.

The large fridge has enough room for a group's groceries, cold drinks for the rooftop and the marinated meat for tonight's BBQ. Families can prepare breakfast exactly the way the kids like it, keep snacks and milk on hand, and skip the daily search for a restaurant that suits everyone. Staying a week or longer? Having a proper kitchen makes a real difference to both comfort and budget.

The dining table by the kitchen windows brings everyone together for the moments that matter on a trip: a slow breakfast before a day out, a shared dinner, a late-night round of cards with a cold drink. And on the evenings when nobody wants to cook, restaurants and street food are close by.

sections.h2: Master bedroom: about 55 m² of calm
p: The master bedroom is a suite in its own right. At about 55 m² it is bigger than many city apartments, with a 180×200 cm bed that leaves plenty of room for two, its own air conditioning and its own private bathroom.

A 55-inch 4K TV lets you finish the evening with a film in bed, and the private balcony is the place for the first coffee of the morning before the rest of the house wakes up. There is a vanity corner for getting ready without rushing, and the house has a safe for passports and valuables, so you can head out without worrying.

It's an easy choice for parents who want a little retreat after a long day with the kids, for a couple celebrating something special, or for whoever organised the trip and has earned the best room. Fresh bedding, towels, toiletries and slippers are ready when you arrive, so all you need to do is unpack.

sections.h2: Bedroom 2: comfort with its own bathroom
p: Bedroom 2 is a comfortable, well-sized room with a 160×200 cm bed, its own air conditioning and its own bathroom. That en-suite bathroom matters more than it sounds: on a family holiday or a trip with friends, it means everyone has their own space, their own shower and their own schedule.

A smart TV with Netflix makes it easy to wind down at the end of the day, whether that's a cartoon for the kids before bedtime or a few episodes of something for the grown-ups. The art wall gives the room a warm, personal feel, more home than hotel.

Bedroom 2 suits a second couple, two siblings or grandparents who want a quiet room of their own while staying close to the rest of the family. Fresh bedding, towels and slippers are ready, hot water is always available, and an iron is on hand if you need to look sharp for a meeting or a dinner out.

sections.h2: Bedroom 3: quiet, dark and made for deep sleep
p: Bedroom 3 is the room for people who take their sleep seriously. It is quiet and naturally dark, so it stays restful even after sunrise. That makes it ideal for jet-lagged travellers who need to sleep in, light sleepers, kids who nap in the afternoon, or anyone who wants to recover properly after a big night of karaoke.
Like the other bedrooms, it has a 160×200 cm bed, its own air conditioning and its own private bathroom. A smart TV with Netflix is there for a quiet evening in.

Fresh bed linen and towels are laid out for you, along with toiletries and slippers. Close the door, set the AC to your favourite temperature and sleep through until you're ready for the day. When you wake up, the kitchen, the living room and the rooftop are only a staircase away.

p: No morning queue, no juggling who showers when. Each of the three bedrooms has its own private bathroom, and there is an extra guest WC in the living area. For families and groups, that alone can make the difference between a stressful morning and a relaxed one.

The bathrooms come with hot water, fresh towels and toiletries, so you can travel light and still feel looked after. The rain showers are the best way to rinse off a day of city heat and humidity before heading out again for dinner.

Because each bathroom belongs to one bedroom, everyone gets their own space to leave their things, get ready at their own pace and keep their routine, whether that's a toddler's bath time or a quick shower before a business meeting. Need fresh clothes for the rest of the trip? A laundry service is available on request.

sections.h2: Karaoke night in your own room
flow: Most karaoke nights in a big city involve booking a room, splitting a taxi and watching the clock. Here you just walk down the hallway. Dim the lights, hand round the microphones and switch on the 4K projector.

The first song is always the hardest, so start with something everyone knows. Soon the room fills up, someone takes over the song list, and the people who swore they would only watch are standing up with a microphone in hand.

Turn it into a proper karaoke competition. Draw names for the running order, set up a judging panel on the sofa, and give points for courage, style and the most dramatic ending. The winner picks the last song of the night. The losers get the cleaning-up and a rematch tomorrow.
Karaoke works across generations. Kids love grabbing the microphone, grandparents finally get to sing the songs from their own youth, and parents can show a side the children have never seen.

sections.h2: Duets: the songs you sing together
flow: Some songs simply need two voices. A duet is the easiest way to bring shy singers into the evening: one strong voice and one hesitant one, and suddenly both are laughing. Parent and child, two old friends from school, a couple who finally get to sing "their" song, colleagues who have never seen each other outside the office.
On a quiet night with just the two of you, the entertainment room becomes your own private karaoke bar. No audience except each other, and nobody to judge if the high notes don't quite land.
Make duets a round in your competition: random pairs, one song each, and the group votes. It mixes people up and creates the stories you'll be telling on the flight home.

sections.h2: When the voices need a break: PlayStation game night
flow: After an hour of singing, switch the big screen over to the PlayStation. With PlayStation Plus there is always something to play, whether you want a head-to-head race, a team effort in a co-op adventure, or a quick group game that even beginners understand in seconds.

A family tournament is the classic: draw up a bracket on a piece of paper, play best of three, and watch the kids beat the adults. It's also a good plan B for a hot afternoon or a rainy day, when everyone needs a break from the city.
After a day of calls on the fast mesh WiFi, a short gaming session is a simple way to switch off before dinner, without leaving the house.

Sometimes the best evening is the quietest one. Lower the lights, settle into the sofas and turn the big screen into a home cinema. Netflix is ready to stream, so the hardest part is agreeing on a film. Make popcorn in the kitchen, grab cold drinks from the large fridge and let the projector do the rest.
A family movie night is a lovely end to a busy day of sightseeing: the kids choose the film, the adults choose the snacks, and half the family is usually asleep before the credits.
Plan a film marathon, a series binge or a quiet date night. It is your room, on your schedule.

sections.h2: Good to know: loud music only until 21:30
flow: The house sits in a residential neighbourhood, and the house rules allow loud music only until 21:30. In practice this works well: sing the big songs in the early evening, then switch to a game or a film as the night goes on. Your neighbours stay friendly, and everyone in the house gets a good night's sleep before the next day in Saigon.

p: ASCON LIVING works best for people who want to travel together without living on top of each other. Families get a private bathroom for every bedroom, a kitchen for easy meals and an entertainment room that keeps kids and teenagers happy. Groups of friends get karaoke, game nights and BBQ evenings on the rooftop. Colleagues on a work trip get fast mesh WiFi, quiet bedrooms and a living room that doubles as a meeting space.
If you're comparing Ho Chi Minh City vacation rentals, this is the difference: one private house, shared only with the people you came with. See our pages for families and for groups for more ideas.

sections.h2: Your own terrace above the city
flow: Climb the stairs to the top of the house and the city opens up. The rooftop terrace measures about 56–60 m² and belongs only to you and the people you are travelling with. In front of you lies the river, and beyond it the skyline of District 1. Many visitors to Ho Chi Minh City see a view like this only from a crowded rooftop bar. Here it comes with the house.
Plants frame the terrace and make it feel green and calm. The outdoor sofa invites you to sit down and stay a while, and the dining area seats everyone together for a meal.
Kids love looking out over the river and the city from above, and parents love having an outdoor space that is completely private.
A quiet corner of the sofa, two drinks and the city in front of you: the rooftop is the most romantic spot in the house.

flow: The rooftop has a BBQ and a smoker, right next to the seating area, so whoever is cooking never misses the conversation. Shop at the market in the afternoon for fresh seafood, skewers and vegetables, keep everything cold in the kitchen fridge of about 540 litres, and carry it up when the sun starts to go down.
A rooftop BBQ is the natural centre of a group trip. One person grills, one person mixes drinks, everyone else finds a seat on the sofa as the lights of District 1 come on across the river.
Grilled corn, chicken skewers and a simple salad: an easy family dinner, eaten outside with a view the kids will remember.
The smoker gives you a reason to start early. Put something on in the afternoon and let it cook slowly while the evening unfolds.

As the sun sets, the sky over the river changes colour and the towers of District 1 light up one by one. The solar lights on the terrace come on by themselves and give the space a soft, warm glow. This is when the rooftop is at its best.
Watch the sunset together and stay on the sofa long after dark.
Raise a glass to a birthday, a reunion or simply a great day in the city.
During the day the rooftop is a peaceful spot. Read a book on the outdoor sofa, have a coffee among the plants, or sit and plan tomorrow's route with the ASCON Guide App.
The mesh WiFi reaches up to 1 Gbit/s on every floor, so a coffee on the rooftop between two video calls is easy to fit in.

sections.h2: Good neighbours: loud music only until 21:30
flow: The house is in a residential area, and the house rules allow loud music only until 21:30. The rooftop is perfect for this rhythm: dinner and drinks in the early evening, then quieter conversations under the solar lights as the night goes on. The view is just as beautiful at a lower volume.

17:30, someone carries the marinated meat and a bowl of salad up the stairs. The BBQ heats up while the others settle on the outdoor sofa. 18:00, the sun is going down over the river and the sky turns orange. 18:30, the first skewers are ready, the solar lights come on and the District 1 skyline starts to glow. Dinner stretches out over hours of conversation. Later, the music goes down, a few people stay up talking quietly, and the city keeps shining across the river.

families.lead: Travelling with kids, grandparents or the whole extended family? At ASCON LIVING you have the entire house to yourselves, with a bathroom for every bedroom and plenty of space to play, eat and rest.

sections.h2: Why families feel at home here
flow: Family trips work best when everyone has room to breathe. In a hotel that usually means two or three separate rooms, often on different floors, and a lot of time in corridors and lifts. At ASCON LIVING the whole family stays under one roof, in a private house with over 250 m² of living space across three floors plus a rooftop terrace. No other guests share the house, so nobody minds if the kids are lively in the morning.
Nap times, early bedtimes and late-night snacks are easy when the kitchen, the living room and the bedrooms are all yours.
Grandparents get their own room and bathroom, close to the family but with their own space.

Their own room, their own TV and their own bathroom: a simple recipe for a happy teenager.

sections.h2: Meals the way your family likes them
flow: Picky eaters, early breakfasts, baby food, a craving for something familiar after a week of new flavours: a real kitchen solves all of that. There is a stove, an oven, a microwave, a rice cooker, a kettle and dishes for everyone, plus a fridge of about 540 litres for milk, fruit, snacks and drinks.
Cook pasta for the kids and try something Vietnamese for yourselves, or bring back food from the restaurants and street food stalls nearby and eat together at the dining table.
On a warm evening, carry dinner up to the rooftop and grill on the BBQ with the river and the District 1 skyline in view.

sections.h2: Rainy afternoons and family movie nights
flow: Every family holiday needs a plan B. The entertainment room turns an afternoon indoors into a highlight: a movie night with the 4K projector and Netflix, a family karaoke contest, or a PlayStation tournament where the kids finally beat their parents. The living room with its L-shaped sofa and 75-inch 4K TV is the second place to gather.
The grown-ups can head up to the rooftop for a quiet drink under the solar lights. Loud music only until 21:30 means everyone gets a good night's sleep.

Cameras are installed outdoors only, never inside. The house has a safe for passports and valuables. Self check-in with a keypad means you can arrive whenever your flight lands, and you receive a key for the outer gate.
Arriving with luggage and tired kids

An airport transfer can be arranged with your booking. Fresh bedding, towels, toiletries, slippers and hot water are ready when you arrive, an iron is on hand, and a laundry service is available for longer stays.
